## What this document is

This reproduces two finished legs of the FLASH-seq ↔ VASA-seq comparison:

1. **the rRNA fraction and its subunit composition**, on both protocols, measured
   by one method; and
2. **the read-length control** that decides whether FLASH-seq's apparent failure
   to detect short RNA species is chemistry or an artefact of 151 nt reads.

It does **not** cover the two legs that are still blocked (full biotype
composition against VASA, and depth-matched detection) — those need step-6
pickles for four libraries that were still building when this was written.
Section 8 says exactly where they stop.

**To run it line by line:** open this `.qmd` in VS Code (Remote-SSH to a NEMO
login node, then `srun --partition=nint --pty --mem=16G bash` for a compute
shell) and execute chunks one at a time. The jupyter bash engine keeps **one
persistent shell** for the whole document, so a variable set in the setup chunk
is still there twenty chunks later — which is the reason for this format. Do not
run the heavy chunks on a login node; the memory cgroup there kills processes
silently.

Every number quoted in the prose below was produced by the chunk above it. Where
a number came from a run that is *not* repeated here (because it takes hours),
the prose says so and gives the job id.

## 1. Setup — paths, versions, and what we are pointing at

Everything downstream refers to these variables, so re-running against a copy of
the data is a one-line edit. `RES` is the only directory this document writes to.

`FSV_FASTQ` is worth noting: it is a **symlink** into `/nemo/stp/sequencing/`,
a different filesystem from the working directory. Anything that globs it needs
`find -L`, or it will stat the link rather than descend into it.

```{bash}
#| label: setup-paths
set -u

PROJ=/nemo/lab/turnerj/working/guangxin/vasaseq
CODE=$PROJ/code
FV=$CODE/flashseq_vasa
RES=$PROJ/res/flashseq_vasa

# --- VASA side: the user's own plate ---

# --- VASA side: the published plate, for reference ---
PUB_BAMS=$PROJ/data/ref/fastq_vasaplate/rrna_validation/unique_rRNA_human_mouse.v2

# --- FLASH-seq side ---
FS_CODE=$CODE/flashseq
FS_META=$FS_CODE/sample_metadata.tsv
FS_RRNA_BWA=$PROJ/res/flashseq/rrna_bwa.tsv

# --- shared reference ---

REF_BED=/nemo/lab/turnerj/working/guangxin/reference/vasaseq/mouse_GRCm39_E116/Mus_musculus.GRCm39.116.homemade_IntronExonTrna.v2.bed

# --- environment ---

mkdir -p "$RES"

```

Versions and reference identity, echoed rather than assumed. Version drift is the
most common reason a re-run diverges and it is invisible unless recorded.

```{bash}
#| label: setup-versions
set -u
source "$CONDA_SH"
conda activate "$VASA_ENV"

python3 -c "import sys, pandas, numpy, pysam; \
print('python  ', sys.version.split()[0]); \
print('pandas  ', pandas.__version__); \
print('numpy   ', numpy.__version__); \
print('pysam   ', pysam.__version__)"

echo ""
echo "rRNA reference : $(md5sum "$RRNA_FA" | cut -c1-32)  $(basename "$RRNA_FA")"
echo "annotation BED : $(md5sum "$REF_BED" | cut -c1-32)  $(basename "$REF_BED")"
echo "genome build   : GRCm39, Ensembl 116"
```

**pandas must stay on 2.x.** The upstream `countTables_fromPickle.py` calls
`DataFrame.applymap`, which was deprecated in pandas 2.1 and **removed in 3.0**.
If a re-run of this document reports pandas 3.x, the count-table stages will
fail; rebuild the env pinned rather than "fixing" the upstream script.

## 2. Why the rRNA numbers are one measurement and not two

This is the load-bearing methodological point of the whole comparison, so it is
worth stating before any code.

The FLASH-seq rRNA fraction was **not** computed with a FLASH-seq-specific tool.
`code/flashseq/05_rrna_bwa.sh` invokes VASA's own `ribo-bwamem.sh` and
`riboread-selection.py`, unmodified, against the same `unique_rRNA_mouse.v2.fa`,
using both `bwa aln` and `bwa mem` exactly as upstream runs them. That was
deliberate: `code/flashseq/config.sh` carries a warning that reimplementing the
measurement would silently create a *second* method, at which point the two
percentages would no longer be comparable.

The classification `riboread-selection.py` performs is small enough to state in
full. Copied verbatim from
`code/I_Gene_expression/a_Mapping/riboread-selection.py` (upstream, unmodified —
`git diff` against its first commit `8bee6f6` shows only a file-mode change):

```{bash}
#| label: show-upstream-predicate
set -u
sed -n '/^for i, r in enumerate/,/^        reads = \[r\]/p' \
    "$CODE/I_Gene_expression/a_Mapping/riboread-selection.py" | head -30
```

Read in prose: alignments are grouped by read name; if **every** alignment in the
group is unmapped the read is not ribosomal and goes to the non-ribosomal arm;
otherwise `stranded='n'` counts it as ribosomal if *any* alignment mapped, and
`stranded='y'` only if an alignment mapped on the **forward** strand.

The grouping matters — a read with several alignments is one observation, not
several — and so does the flag, which is the next section.

---

## 3. The strand flag, and why the two protocols use different ones

`stranded=y` is correct for VASA and wrong for FLASH-seq, and this is measured
rather than assumed.

```{bash}
#| label: strand-flag-provenance
set -u
echo "=== what the user's own VASA run used ==="
grep -n -B1 "^STRANDED=" "$CODE/I_Gene_expression/own_version/config.sh"

echo ""
echo "=== what the published VASA code specifies ==="
grep -n "^STRANDED=" "$CODE/I_Gene_expression/a_Mapping/run_mapping_stepwise.sh"
grep -n 'set to "y"' "$CODE/I_Gene_expression/a_Mapping/README.md"

echo ""
echo "=== FLASH-seq forward-strand share of ribosomal reads (measured) ==="
awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) h[$i]=i; next}
            $h["arm"]=="trimmed"{printf "  %-12s fwd_pct=%s\n", $h["library"]?$1:$1, $(h["fwd_pct"])}' \
    "$FS_RRNA_BWA" | head -10
```

FLASH-seq's ribosomal reads are split ~50/50 between strands, which is what an
unstranded library should show. Applying `y` there would discard roughly half of
its genuine ribosomal reads and report half the true rRNA content — penalising it
for its chemistry rather than measuring its rRNA.

**Decision (user, 2026-07-28): each protocol keeps its own correct flag** — VASA
`y`, FLASH-seq `n`. The resulting ratio must always be quoted as *"each protocol
under its own correct flag"*, never as a bare division. Section 5 gives the
sensitivity to that choice.

---

## 4. Re-deriving the VASA rRNA fractions from the BAMs

The step-3 log already reports a per-cell `ribo%`, but a number in a log is not a
reproducible measurement. This chunk recomputes both predicates from the
`.nsorted.all-ribo.bam` files and **asserts** the result against the log — if the
predicate implemented here is not the one `riboread-selection.py` applied, this
fails loudly rather than producing a plausible wrong number.

The script is `verify_rrna_crossplate.py`, committed in `flashseq_vasa/`. It is
reproduced here in full rather than pointed at, so this document stands alone.

```{bash}
#| label: write-verify-script
set -u
cat > "$RES/verify_rrna_crossplate_runbook.py" <<'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Re-derive every cross-plate rRNA number from the BAMs and assert it.

classify() is copied from ../I_Gene_expression/a_Mapping/riboread-selection.py so
that what is tested is what upstream executed. It reproduces the classification
only: the source also writes the fastq/bam and counts per-reference hits, none of
which is needed for the fractions.
"""
import os, sys, re, glob
import pysam


def classify(group):
    """-> (is_ribo_n, is_ribo_y) for one read's alignment group."""
    if all(r.is_unmapped for r in group):
        return (False, False)
    ribo_n = True                                     # stranded='n': any mapped
    ribo_y = any((not r.is_unmapped) and (not r.is_reverse) for r in group)
    return (ribo_n, ribo_y)


def count_bam(path):
    bam = pysam.AlignmentFile(path, check_sq=False)
    total = n_any = n_fwd = 0
    cur, grp = None, []
    for r in bam.fetch(until_eof=True):
        if cur is None or r.qname == cur:
            grp.append(r); cur = r.qname
        else:
            total += 1
            a, f = classify(grp); n_any += a; n_fwd += f
            grp = [r]; cur = r.qname
    if grp:
        total += 1
        a, f = classify(grp); n_any += a; n_fwd += f
    bam.close()
    return total, n_any, n_fwd


def parse_step3_log(path):
    want = re.compile(r'^\s*(\d{3})\s+([\d,]+)\s+([\d,]+)\s+([\d.]+)%')
    out = {}
    for line in open(path):
        m = want.match(line)
        if m:
            out[m.group(1)] = float(m.group(4))
    return out


def summarise(d, label, blanks=()):
    real = {k: v for k, v in d.items() if k not in blanks}
    py = sorted(v['pct_y'] for v in real.values())
    fw = sorted(v['fwd'] for v in real.values())
    med = lambda a: a[len(a)//2] if len(a) % 2 else 0.5*(a[len(a)//2-1]+a[len(a)//2])
    tot = sum(v['total'] for v in d.values())
    ry = sum(v['ribo_y'] for v in d.values())
    print(f"{label}")
    print(f"    n={len(real)}  pct_y  min={py[0]:.3f}  median={med(py):.3f}  max={py[-1]:.3f}")
    print(f"              fwd    min={fw[0]:.2f}   median={med(fw):.2f}   max={fw[-1]:.2f}")
    print(f"    read-weighted over ALL entries: {100*ry/tot:.3f}%  ({ry:,} / {tot:,})")
    return dict(median_y=med(py), min_y=py[0], max_y=py[-1],
                median_fwd=med(fw), weighted=100*ry/tot)


def collect(pattern, idre):
    out = {}
    for b in sorted(glob.glob(pattern)):
        m = re.search(idre, os.path.basename(b))
        cc = m.group(1) if m else os.path.basename(b)
        t, na, nf = count_bam(b)
        out[cc] = dict(total=t, ribo_n=na, ribo_y=nf,
                       pct_n=100.0*na/t if t else 0.0,
                       pct_y=100.0*nf/t if t else 0.0,
                       fwd=100.0*nf/na if na else 0.0)
    return out


def main():
    own_dir, pub_dir, step3_log, outdir = sys.argv[1:5]
    fail = []

    own = collect(os.path.join(own_dir, '*.nsorted.all-ribo.bam'), r'_(\d{3})_')
    pub = collect(os.path.join(pub_dir, '*.nsorted.all-ribo.bam'), r'_(\d{3})\.')

    print("=" * 74)
    print("CHECK: does our stranded=y predicate reproduce step3.log?")
    print("=" * 74)
    log = parse_step3_log(step3_log)
    worst = 0.0
    for cc in sorted(log):
        if cc not in own:
            continue
        d = abs(own[cc]['pct_y'] - log[cc])
        worst = max(worst, d)
        print(f"  {'x' if d > 0.01 else ' '} {cc}  ours={own[cc]['pct_y']:7.3f}"
              f"  log={log[cc]:7.3f}  |diff|={d:.4f}")
    print(f"  worst |deviation| = {worst:.4f} percentage points")
    if worst > 0.01:
        fail.append(f"predicate does not reproduce step3.log (worst {worst:.4f} pp)")
    else:
        print("  -> PASS: same predicate, to within log rounding.")

    BLANKS = {'001', '014', '015', '016'}
    print()
    print("=" * 74)
    print("MEASUREMENTS")
    print("=" * 74)
    o = summarise(own, "VASA own plate (blanks excluded from per-cell stats)", BLANKS)
    print()
    p = summarise(pub, "VASA published plate SRR14783059")

    print()
    print("=" * 74)
    print("DERIVED RATIOS -- state which one you mean; they are not interchangeable")
    print("=" * 74)
    print(f"  median ratio (own / published) = {o['median_y']/p['median_y']:.3f}x")
    print(f"  pooled ratio (own / published) = {o['weighted']/p['weighted']:.3f}x")
    ps = p['max_y']/p['min_y']; os_ = o['max_y']/o['min_y']
    print(f"  spread published = {ps:.2f}x   own = {os_:.2f}x   own tighter by {ps/os_:.1f}x")
    print("  (the two ratios differ because the published cells span 64k-1.26M reads,")
    print("   so pooling weights the deep cells)")

    for name, d in (('verify_own_percell.tsv', own),
                    ('verify_published_percell.tsv', pub)):
        with open(os.path.join(outdir, name), 'w') as fh:
            fh.write('cell\ttotal\tribo_n\tribo_y\tpct_n\tpct_y\tfwd_share\n')
            for cc in sorted(d):
                v = d[cc]
                fh.write(f"{cc}\t{v['total']}\t{v['ribo_n']}\t{v['ribo_y']}"
                         f"\t{v['pct_n']:.4f}\t{v['pct_y']:.4f}\t{v['fwd']:.2f}\n")
        print(f"\nwrote {name} ({len(d)} rows)")

    print()
    if fail:
        print("FAIL:")
        for f in fail:
            print("  x", f)
        sys.exit(1)
    print("PASS -- every number above is reproduced from the BAMs.")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
PYEOF
echo "wrote $RES/verify_rrna_crossplate_runbook.py"
```

This reads every `.nsorted.all-ribo.bam` on both plates, so it wants a compute
node rather than a login shell. It took about 12 minutes as job `0f559630`.

```{bash}
#| label: run-verify
set -u
source "$CONDA_SH"; conda activate "$VASA_ENV"

python3 "$RES/verify_rrna_crossplate_runbook.py" \
    "$VASA_CELLS" "$PUB_BAMS" "$VASA_STEP3_LOG" "$RES" \
    | tee "$RES/verify_runbook.txt"
```

**What that output establishes.** The predicate reimplemented here reproduces
step 3's own `ribo%` for **all 16 barcodes to within 0.005 percentage points** —
that is the check that makes every other figure in this section trustworthy,
because it proves the classification is upstream's and not merely a plausible
one.

The user's own plate reads **21.14% median** across its 12 real cells
(17.99–25.09%), and **21.39%** read-weighted over all 16 barcodes. The published
plate reads **9.90% median** (1.33–26.42%), **9.19%** pooled.

So this plate carries about **2.1× more rRNA on medians** (2.33× pooled) than the
published one — but with a **14× tighter spread** across cells. Both facts
matter: a high mean with a tight spread is a systematic offset, which is the kind
of thing that can be tuned; a low mean with a 20-fold spread is variable
depletion. Note also that the two ratios differ because the published cells span
64 k–1.26 M reads, so pooling weights the deep ones. Say which you mean.

**Caveat that must travel with the 2.1×:** the published side is the 8 cells a
prior session pulled for rRNA-reference validation, not a random sample of the
published experiment, and it was run against the human/mouse mixed reference
where this plate used mouse-only. Real signal, provisional magnitude.

---

## 5. Assembling the rRNA comparison table

Now the FLASH-seq side joins in. The FLASH-seq figures come from
`res/flashseq/rrna_bwa.tsv`, produced by `05_rrna_bwa.sh` as job `50855065` —
that run streams every FASTQ through `bwa` twice and is not repeated here; it
takes about 46 minutes.

Every row of the output table carries its strand flag and the rationale for it,
so no downstream reader can compare two rows that were counted differently
without noticing.

```{bash}
#| label: build-rrna-table
set -u
source "$CONDA_SH"; conda activate "$VASA_ENV"

cat > "$RES/mk_rrna_comparison.py" <<'PYEOF'
import sys
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

FS_RRNA_BWA, FS_META, RES = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]

fs = pd.read_csv(FS_RRNA_BWA, sep='\t')
fs.columns = [c.strip() for c in fs.columns]
meta = pd.read_csv(FS_META, sep='\t', comment='#')
own = pd.read_csv(f'{RES}/verify_own_percell.tsv', sep='\t', dtype={'cell': str})
pub = pd.read_csv(f'{RES}/verify_published_percell.tsv', sep='\t', dtype={'cell': str})

# the trimmed arm is the one that fed everything downstream
fst = fs[fs.arm.astype(str).str.strip() == 'trimmed'].copy()
qcv = meta.set_index('library').qc_verdict.to_dict()
BLANK = {'001', '014', '015', '016'}
rows = []

for _, r in fst.iterrows():
    rows.append(dict(
        dataset='FLASH-seq RN26038', unit=r.library, group=str(r.input_amount).strip(),
        well=r.well, reads_in=int(r.reads_in), rrna_pct=float(r.ribo_pct),
        strand_flag='n',
        flag_rationale='unstranded library; forward strand carries %.1f%% of ribosomal reads' % r.fwd_pct,
        rrna_pct_other_flag=float(r.ribo_pct_stranded_y),
        pct_5ETS=float(r['pct_5ETS']), pct_18S=float(r['pct_18S']),
        pct_ITS1=float(r['pct_ITS1']), pct_5_8S=float(r['pct_5.8S']),
        pct_ITS2=float(r['pct_ITS2']), pct_28S=float(r['pct_28S']),
        pct_mito=float(r['pct_mito']), pct_other=float(r['pct_other']),
        qc_verdict=qcv.get(r.library, ''),
        source='res/flashseq/rrna_bwa.tsv (trimmed arm), job 50855065'))

for _, r in own.iterrows():
    blank = r.cell in BLANK
    rows.append(dict(
        dataset='VASA ZHA9292A1 (own)', unit='cell_%s' % r.cell,
        group='blank' if blank else 'real cell', well='',
        reads_in=int(r.total), rrna_pct=float(r.pct_y), strand_flag='y',
        flag_rationale='stranded protocol; the published VASA code specifies y (fwd share %.1f%%)' % r.fwd_share,
        rrna_pct_other_flag=float(r.pct_n),
        pct_5ETS=np.nan, pct_18S=np.nan, pct_ITS1=np.nan, pct_5_8S=np.nan,
        pct_ITS2=np.nan, pct_28S=np.nan, pct_mito=np.nan, pct_other=np.nan,
        qc_verdict='exclude (confirmed blank)' if blank else 'ok',
        source='verify_rrna_crossplate.py; reproduces step3.log to 0.005pp'))

for _, r in pub.iterrows():
    rows.append(dict(
        dataset='VASA SRR14783059 (published)', unit='cell_%s' % r.cell,
        group='published cell', well='',
        reads_in=int(r.total), rrna_pct=float(r.pct_y), strand_flag='y',
        flag_rationale='stranded protocol (fwd share %.1f%%)' % r.fwd_share,
        rrna_pct_other_flag=float(r.pct_n),
        pct_5ETS=np.nan, pct_18S=np.nan, pct_ITS1=np.nan, pct_5_8S=np.nan,
        pct_ITS2=np.nan, pct_28S=np.nan, pct_mito=np.nan, pct_other=np.nan,
        qc_verdict='reference',
        source='verify_rrna_crossplate.py; human/mouse mixed rRNA reference'))

rr = pd.DataFrame(rows)
rr.to_csv(f'{RES}/rrna_comparison.tsv', sep='\t', index=False)

def agg(m, label):
    d = rr[m]
    return dict(subset=label, n=len(d), min=round(d.rrna_pct.min(), 3),
                median=round(d.rrna_pct.median(), 3), max=round(d.rrna_pct.max(), 3),
                read_weighted_pct=round((d.rrna_pct*d.reads_in).sum()/d.reads_in.sum(), 3),
                total_reads=int(d.reads_in.sum()))

isFS = rr.dataset.str.startswith('FLASH')
summ = pd.DataFrame([
    agg(isFS & (rr.qc_verdict != 'exclude'), 'FLASH-seq, 9 libraries (A8 excluded), stranded=n'),
    agg(isFS, 'FLASH-seq, all 10 incl. A8, stranded=n'),
    agg(isFS & (rr.group == '30 pg'), 'FLASH-seq 30 pg rung A9+A10, stranded=n'),
    agg(rr.dataset.str.contains('own') & (rr.group == 'real cell'), 'VASA own, 12 real cells, stranded=y'),
    agg(rr.dataset.str.contains('own'), 'VASA own, all 16 barcodes, stranded=y'),
    agg(rr.dataset.str.contains('published'), 'VASA published, 8 cells, stranded=y'),
])
summ.to_csv(f'{RES}/rrna_comparison_summary.tsv', sep='\t', index=False)
print(summ.to_string(index=False))

fs9 = rr[isFS & (rr.qc_verdict != 'exclude')]
ov = rr[rr.dataset.str.contains('own') & (rr.group == 'real cell')]
print()
print('HEADLINE -- each protocol under its OWN correct flag:')
print('  VASA (y)      median %.2f%%  range %.2f-%.2f%%'
      % (ov.rrna_pct.median(), ov.rrna_pct.min(), ov.rrna_pct.max()))
print('  FLASH-seq (n) median %.2f%%  range %.2f-%.2f%%'
      % (fs9.rrna_pct.median(), fs9.rrna_pct.min(), fs9.rrna_pct.max()))
print('  ratio of medians = %.2fx' % (ov.rrna_pct.median()/fs9.rrna_pct.median()))
print()
print('SENSITIVITY to the flag pairing (both figures measured, not assumed):')
print('  VASA y / FS n  (each correct)  = %.2fx' % (ov.rrna_pct.median()/fs9.rrna_pct.median()))
print('  both n                         = %.2fx'
      % (ov.rrna_pct_other_flag.median()/fs9.rrna_pct.median()))
print('  both y                         = %.2fx'
      % (ov.rrna_pct.median()/fs9.rrna_pct_other_flag.median()))
print()
print('SELF-CHECK: all-16 read-weighted must reproduce step3.log whole-library 21.39%%')
w = summ[summ.subset.str.contains('all 16')].read_weighted_pct.iloc[0]
print('  computed %.3f%%  ->  %s' % (w, 'MATCH' if abs(w-21.39) < 0.02 else 'MISMATCH'))

print()
print('FLASH-seq subunit composition, %% of ribosomal reads (9 libraries):')
for col, lab in [('pct_5ETS', "5'ETS"), ('pct_28S', '28S'), ('pct_18S', '18S'),
                 ('pct_ITS2', 'ITS2'), ('pct_ITS1', 'ITS1'), ('pct_5_8S', '5.8S'),
                 ('pct_mito', 'mito'), ('pct_other', 'other')]:
    v = fs9[col].dropna()
    print('  %-6s %6.2f - %6.2f   median %6.2f' % (lab, v.min(), v.max(), v.median()))
print()
print('rows written: %d' % len(rr))
PYEOF

python3 "$RES/mk_rrna_comparison.py" "$FS_RRNA_BWA" "$FS_META" "$RES" \
    | tee "$RES/rrna_comparison_report.txt"
```

**The headline.** FLASH-seq **4.70%** median (3.50–6.44%, 9 libraries with A8
excluded) against this VASA plate's **21.14%** (17.99–25.09%, 12 real cells) =
**4.50×**.

The sensitivity block shows why the flag pairing had to be a stated decision
rather than a default: the same two datasets give **4.50×** with each protocol
under its own correct flag, **6.08×** with both `n`, and **8.95×** with both `y`.
The flag alone moves the answer by a factor of two.

The self-check line is there so the table cannot silently drift: the read-weighted
all-16-barcode figure is recomputed by a different route from step 3's own
whole-library number and must land on **21.39%**.

**Where the residual rRNA sits.** Most of what survives poly-A selection in
FLASH-seq is **pre-rRNA, not mature rRNA** — 5'ETS is the largest segment at
~41% of ribosomal reads, against 28S at ~26%. That is mechanistically sensible:
the 47S precursor is transient and carries non-templated ends, so it is more
poly-A-accessible than mature 28S. It also locates the protocol gap in mature
28S, which is precisely where VASA's in-silico depletion has the most to remove.

**Do not use the annotation route for rRNA.** Ensembl's `rRNA` biotype reads
0.47–1.40% where this alignment route reads 3.50–6.44%. On GRCm39 the rDNA array
is collapsed out of the primary assembly, so there is no `Rn45s`, `Rn28s` or
`Rn5-8s` gene, and 99.93–99.999% of that class's signal comes from a single 18S
relic locus, `Rn18s-rs5` (`ENSMUSG00000119584`).

```{bash}
#| label: rrna-biotype-is-not-rrna
set -u
GTF=/nemo/lab/turnerj/working/guangxin/reference/genomes/mus_musculus/GRCm39/annotation/release-116/gtf/Mus_musculus.GRCm39.116.gtf
awk -F'\t' '$3=="gene" && $9~/gene_biotype "rRNA"/' "$GTF" \
  | grep -o 'gene_name "[^"]*"' | sed 's/gene_name //; s/"//g' \
  | sed 's/[0-9-]*$//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -6
echo ""
echo "Rn45s / Rn28s / Rn5-8s present in the rRNA biotype?"
awk -F'\t' '$3=="gene" && $9~/gene_biotype "rRNA"/' "$GTF" \
  | grep -cE 'gene_name "(Rn45s|Rn28s|Rn5-8s)"' || echo "0  (as expected)"
```

---

## 6. The read-length control

### Why it was necessary

The naive result was that FLASH-seq detects **zero tRNA**. That is not a finding
about chemistry.

VASA's assignment rule `jS:IN` requires a read to be **contained within** the
annotated feature. At 151 nt a FLASH-seq read cannot sit inside most small RNAs.
Measure that directly against the annotation both protocols share:

```{bash}
#| label: feature-lengths-vs-read-length
set -u
zcat -f "$REF_BED" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '
  {
    n = split($4, a, "_"); bt = a[n]; len = $3 - $2
    tot[bt]++; if (len < 151) short[bt]++
  }
  END {
    printf "%-10s %8s %8s %7s\n", "biotype", "features", "<151nt", "pct"
    split("tRNA rRNA miRNA snoRNA snRNA ProteinCoding lncRNA", want, " ")
    for (i in want) {
      bt = want[i]
      if (tot[bt] > 0)
        printf "%-10s %8d %8d %6.1f%%\n", bt, tot[bt], short[bt], 100*short[bt]/tot[bt]
    }
  }'
```

So a 151 nt library reports few or no reads for these classes **whatever the
chemistry did**. Without a control, "FLASH-seq detects fewer short species" is
unfalsifiable — and it is half of what the comparison was asked to answer.

### The design

Both arms were quantified through VASA's own step 4–7, identical in every setting
**except read length**:

- **`native`** — adapter-trimmed R1 at its natural length
- **`vasalen`** — additionally hard-trimmed to VASA's aligned-length distribution

The target distribution was measured from VASA's own STAR-input FASTQs rather than
assumed from the ~23.7 nt mean in the step-3 log:

```{bash}
#| label: vasa-target-length
set -u
head -25 "$RES/vasa_readlen_report.txt" 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "(vasa_readlen_report.txt not present -- produced by measure_vasa_readlen.py)"
```

Three constraints from the dry run govern how both arms are run, and each would
have wasted the ten-library pass if discovered late. They are recorded in
`flashseq_vasa/NOUMI_PATH.md`; the essential ones are:

- **Map R1 only.** `bedtools bamtobed` appends `/1`,`/2` to paired-end read names,
  and `deal_with_*mappers.sh` appends `;CG:…;nM:<n>` *before* bamtobed runs, so
  the mate suffix lands on the end of the `nM` value and step 6's `int()` raises.
  Measured 1,033,528 of 1,033,528 PE rows unparseable against 0 of 534,978 SE.
  This is upstream's contract, so `a_Mapping/` is not patched.
- **Use `ReadCounts` only.** With one literal UMI key `'A'`, `UFICounts`
  degenerates to a 0/1 detection mask and `bc2trans` is the identity on a mask,
  so `TranscriptCounts == UFICounts` elementwise. Both are still written and
  carry no abundance information.
- **`stranded=n`, `filt_unigenes=n`, `CELLID_FROM=f`** with `_cbc` in the stem.

### The measurement

The mapping and step-6 stages behind this take 7–10 hours per library, so they
are not re-run here. The chunk below reads their output and computes the
comparison. Non-executable reproduction commands for the heavy stages are in
section 8.

```{bash}
#| label: shortbiotype-recovery
set -u
source "$CONDA_SH"; conda activate "$VASA_ENV"

cat > "$RES/mk_shortbiotype.py" <<'PYEOF'
import os, sys
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

S, RES, TAG = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
SHORT = ['tRNA', 'miRNA', 'snoRNA', 'snRNA', 'MiscRna', 'ribozyme', 'scaRNA']
rows, comp = [], []

for arm in ('native', 'vasalen'):
    f = f'{S}/{arm}/{TAG}_{arm}_total.ReadCounts.tsv'
    if not os.path.exists(f):
        print('MISSING', f)
        continue
    df = pd.read_csv(f, sep='\t', index_col=0)
    df.columns = [c.replace('cells/', '') for c in df.columns]
    bio = pd.Series([str(i).rsplit('_', 1)[-1] if '_' in str(i) else 'NA'
                     for i in df.index], index=df.index)
    # non-rRNA denominator: the user's decision is rRNA as % of all reads,
    # every other class as % of the non-rRNA remainder
    nonr = df[~bio.isin(['rRNA', 'Mt_rRNA'])]
    tot = nonr.values.sum()
    print(f'\n=== arm={arm}  entries={len(df)}  libraries={list(df.columns)}')
    print(f'    non-rRNA denominator = {tot:,.0f} reads')
    for b in SHORT:
        m = bio == b
        n_e = int(m.sum())
        rd = float(df[m].values.sum()) if n_e else 0.0
        det = int((df[m].sum(axis=1) > 0).sum()) if n_e else 0
        rows.append(dict(arm=arm, biotype=b, entries=n_e, entries_detected=det,
                         reads=rd, pct_of_nonrRNA=100*rd/tot if tot else 0))
        print(f'  {b:9s} entries={n_e:6d} detected={det:6d} reads={rd:12,.0f}'
              f'  {100*rd/tot if tot else 0:8.4f}% of non-rRNA')
    for b, g in nonr.groupby(bio[nonr.index]):
        comp.append(dict(arm=arm, biotype=b, reads=float(g.values.sum()),
                         pct_of_nonrRNA=100*float(g.values.sum())/tot))

if not rows:
    sys.exit('no arm tables found -- run the mapping stages first')

sb = pd.DataFrame(rows)
p = sb.pivot(index='biotype', columns='arm', values=['entries_detected', 'reads', 'pct_of_nonrRNA'])
det, rds = p['entries_detected'], p['reads']
out = pd.DataFrame({
    'native_detected': det['native'].astype(int),
    'vasalen_detected': det['vasalen'].astype(int),
    'fold_entries': (det['vasalen']/det['native'].replace(0, np.nan)).round(2),
    'native_reads': rds['native'].astype(int),
    'vasalen_reads': rds['vasalen'].astype(int),
    'fold_reads': (rds['vasalen']/rds['native'].replace(0, np.nan)).round(2),
    'native_pct_nonrRNA': p['pct_of_nonrRNA']['native'].round(4),
    'vasalen_pct_nonrRNA': p['pct_of_nonrRNA']['vasalen'].round(4),
}).sort_values('fold_entries', ascending=False)
out.to_csv(f'{RES}/shortbiotype_readlength6.tsv', sep='\t')
print()
print('=== short-biotype recovery, native -> VASA-matched length ===')
print(out.to_string())

cc = pd.DataFrame(comp).pivot(index='biotype', columns='arm', values='pct_of_nonrRNA').fillna(0)
cc['delta_pp'] = (cc.vasalen - cc.native).round(3)
cc.to_csv(f'{RES}/composition6_nonrRNA.tsv', sep='\t')
print()
print('=== composition on the non-rRNA denominator (top 10) ===')
print(cc.sort_values('native', ascending=False).head(10).round(3).to_string())
PYEOF

python3 "$RES/mk_shortbiotype.py" "$FS_SCRATCH" "$RES" FSprov6 \
    | tee "$RES/shortbiotype_report.txt"
```

**Result: length-matching recovers much of the gap.** Six libraries are complete
in both arms (A1, A3, A4, A5, A8, A9 — including A9, the 30 pg
single-cell-equivalent rung). Entries detected rise **1.5–2.2×** when reads are
trimmed to VASA's length: ribozyme 2.20×, snRNA 1.87×, miRNA 1.86×, snoRNA 1.70×,
MiscRna 1.64×, scaRNA 1.50×.

The conclusion is **stable under the n=4 → n=6 upgrade** — every fold moved by
≤0.30 and the ordering is essentially unchanged, which is the check that matters
for a result reported before all ten libraries were in.

One nuance worth keeping: *MiscRna* recovers **entries** (1.64×) but not **reads**
(0.96×). Trimming finds more distinct loci while splitting the same read mass
across them, so for abundant classes "recovery" means detection breadth, not extra
signal.

### The mechanism, measured directly

If read length is the cause, then trimming should move both the read-length
distribution *and* the containment rate toward VASA. It does:

```{bash}
#| label: containment-mechanism
set -u
source "$CONDA_SH"; conda activate "$VASA_ENV"

cat > "$RES/lenchk.py" <<'PYEOF'
import glob, gzip, sys
import numpy as np

def stats(pattern, label, cap=500000):
    fs = sorted(glob.glob(pattern))
    if not fs:
        print(f'{label}: NO FILES  ({pattern})')
        return None
    L, jsin, n = [], 0, 0
    for f in fs:
        with gzip.open(f, 'rt') as fh:
            for line in fh:
                p = line.rstrip('\n').split('\t')
                if len(p) < 3:
                    continue
                L.append(int(p[2]) - int(p[1])); n += 1
                if ';jS:IN' in line:
                    jsin += 1
                if n >= cap:
                    break
        if n >= cap:
            break
    a = np.array(L)
    print(label)
    print(f'    n={len(a):,}  median={np.median(a):.0f}')
    print(f'    >=140nt: {100*(a>=140).mean():5.1f}%    jS:IN rate: {100*jsin/n:5.1f}%')
    return a

S, V = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
print('=== aligned length of the BED rows that fed step 6 (library A9) ===')
stats(f'{S}/native/pickle/ZHA8833A9/cells/*singlemappers_genes.bed.gz',  'FLASH-seq A9  native')
stats(f'{S}/vasalen/pickle/ZHA8833A9/cells/*singlemappers_genes.bed.gz', 'FLASH-seq A9  VASA-trimmed')
stats(f'{V}/*_005_*singlemappers_genes.bed.gz',                          'VASA cell 005')
PYEOF

python3 "$RES/lenchk.py" "$FS_SCRATCH" "$VASA_CELLS" | tee "$RES/readlen_check.txt"
```

Reads `≥140 nt` fall from **82.4%** to **55.4%** against VASA's **44.5%**, and the
`jS:IN` containment rate rises from **45.7%** to **52.0%** against VASA's
**55.7%**. Both move in the predicted direction.

### What this licenses, and what it does not

**Established:** the mechanism operates and it is large. A 151 nt library
under-reports short RNA classes for reasons that have nothing to do with the
protocol's chemistry.

**Not established:** that read length explains the *whole* gap. Recovery is
partial — the trimmed arm still sits short of VASA on both metrics, and tRNA
remains absent from the biotype scan even though the dedicated tRNA table nearly
doubled (27 → 46 rows, 361 → 754 reads at n=4).

**So the short-species axis is confounded, not resolved.** "FLASH-seq detects
fewer short non-poly-A RNAs than VASA" is **not** a claim this data supports yet.
What it supports is: *at matched read length FLASH-seq still detects fewer, but
the native-length difference overstates it by roughly 1.4–2.5× depending on
class.*

---

## 7. Composition on the non-rRNA denominator — partial

The chunk in section 6 also wrote `composition6_nonrRNA.tsv`. On six libraries,
FLASH-seq is **84.15%** protein-coding of non-rRNA reads at native length, which
is what a poly-A library should look like.

The number to carry forward is not that one, though — it is the **Δ pp** column.
Read length **alone** moves ProteinCoding by **−2.6 pp** and pushes the
pseudogene classes up, because shorter reads are less uniquely assignable so some
protein-coding mass redistributes to paralogous pseudogenes.

**Therefore: any FLASH-seq↔VASA composition difference smaller than about 3 pp is
inside the read-length effect and must not be attributed to protocol.**

The VASA side of this comparison is still missing, and one decision is already
settled for when it lands: **use the unfiltered `uniagg` VASA tables**, not
`data/PM26037/out/analysis/`. The UMI-ceiling filter there drops 8 entries —
*Rmrp*, *Rn7sk*, *Rn7s1*/*Rn7s2*, *Rnu1a1*, *Rnu1b6*, *Rnu2.10*, the *Snord3b*
cluster and a *Cmss1* pair — carrying **23.02% of uniagg reads**, whose removal
shifts ProteinCoding by **+19.19 pp**. They were selected precisely *for*
saturating the UMI ceiling, i.e. for being the most abundant small RNAs, which is
what a total-RNA protocol exists to capture. Correct for molecule counting, wrong
for a reads-vs-reads comparison.

---

## 8. The heavy stages — not executed here

These produced the inputs section 6 reads. They are **not** in a runnable chunk
because each takes hours and the last four libraries were still building when this
was written. Reproduction commands, for completeness:

```bash
# One arm at a time. FSV_ARM selects the read-length treatment; every other
# setting is identical between arms, which is what makes the comparison a control.
cd /nemo/lab/turnerj/working/guangxin/vasaseq

for ARM in native vasalen; do
  FSV_ARM=$ARM code/flashseq_vasa/pipeline_fs.sh check     # config + input validation
  FSV_ARM=$ARM code/flashseq_vasa/pipeline_fs.sh prep      # cutadapt (+ hard-trim for vasalen)
  FSV_ARM=$ARM code/flashseq_vasa/pipeline_fs.sh map       # STAR, R1 only, star_index_151_r116
  FSV_ARM=$ARM code/flashseq_vasa/pipeline_fs.sh assign    # deal_with_{single,multi}mappers.sh, stranded=n
  FSV_ARM=$ARM code/flashseq_vasa/pipeline_fs.sh pickle1   # step 6, ONE LIBRARY AT A TIME
  FSV_ARM=$ARM code/flashseq_vasa/pipeline_fs.sh pickle_merge
  FSV_ARM=$ARM code/flashseq_vasa/pipeline_fs.sh tables    # step 7, protocol=smartseq_noUMI
  FSV_ARM=$ARM code/flashseq_vasa/pipeline_fs.sh recon
done
```

**Observed resource use**, so a re-run can be sized rather than guessed:

| stage | observed |
|---|---|
| step 6, per library | 7 h 40 m – 10 h 05 m wall, 39–59 GB MaxRSS |
| step 6, 6 concurrent on one node | ~220 GB RSS against a 650 G request |
| step 7 (VASA side, 16 barcodes) | 32 m, 13.0 GB — a 200 G request was 15× over |
| `05_rrna_bwa.sh` (job `50855065`) | 46 m, 778 MB |

Step 6 is **superlinear in BED size** (69 MB → 28 m; 254 MB → 1 h 47 m on the
VASA side), which is why it is run per library and merged rather than in one pass:
eight libraries resident at once would be ~250 GB in a single process, and any
failure would lose the whole run.

`merge_pickles.py` reproduces upstream step 6's parent tail exactly — the union of
per-library dicts **is** the frame a combined run would have built, because
`get_cellDict` is per-library independent. It asserts the three properties that
make the equivalence hold (disjoint column keys, non-empty inputs, unioned row
keys) rather than assuming them.

## 9. What may and may not be claimed

**May be claimed:**

- FLASH-seq carries about **4.5× less rRNA** than this VASA plate, measured by one
  method, each protocol under its own correct strand flag. State the flags.
- Most of FLASH-seq's residual rRNA is **pre-rRNA (5'ETS ~41% of ribosomal
  reads)**, not mature 28S (~26%).
- This VASA plate carries **~2.1× more rRNA than the published plate** on medians,
  with a **14× tighter spread** — a systematic offset rather than variable
  depletion. Provisional magnitude (8 non-random published cells, mixed
  reference).
- Read length **materially suppresses** short-RNA detection at 151 nt: matching
  VASA's length recovers **1.5–2.2×** more entries.

**May not be claimed:**

- That FLASH-seq detects fewer short non-poly-A RNAs **because of its chemistry**.
  Recovery on length-matching is partial, so the axis is confounded.
- Any composition difference against VASA smaller than **~3 pp**, which is inside
  the read-length effect.
- Anything from `TranscriptCounts` or `UFICounts` on the FLASH-seq side — they are
  a detection mask, not abundance.
- Any rRNA figure from the Ensembl `rRNA` biotype; on GRCm39 that class is
  essentially one 18S relic locus.

```{bash}
#| label: phase-complete
set -u
echo "outputs in $RES:"
ls -1 "$RES"/rrna_comparison*.tsv "$RES"/shortbiotype_readlength6.tsv \
      "$RES"/composition6_nonrRNA.tsv "$RES"/verify_*_percell.tsv 2>/dev/null \
  | sed 's|.*/|  |'
echo ""
echo "PHASE_COMPLETE"
```

## Appendix: approaches tried and rejected

Kept because each cost real time and the reasoning decays fastest.

### Paired-end mapping through VASA's step 5–6
Discarded, structurally. `bedtools bamtobed` appends `/1`,`/2` to the read name
and `deal_with_*mappers.sh` appends `;CG:…;nM:<n>` before bamtobed runs, so the
mate suffix lands on the end of the `nM` value and step 6's `int()` raises.
Measured **1,033,528 of 1,033,528 PE rows unparseable** against 0 of 534,978 SE.
Upstream's contract, so `a_Mapping/` was not patched — R1 only.

### The Ensembl `rRNA` biotype as the rRNA measurement
Reads 0.47–1.40% against 3.50–6.44% from alignment. The rDNA array is collapsed
out of GRCm39's primary assembly, and 99.93–99.999% of that biotype's signal is
one 18S relic locus (`Rn18s-rs5`). Also documented once as "essentially all 5S" —
**that was wrong**, and the correction is in `NFCORE_CROSSCHECK.md`.

### `TranscriptCounts` from the `smartseq_noUMI` path
Discarded as meaningless, but not for the reason first assumed. `bc2trans` is
applied to the UFI table, not to read counts — and with one literal UMI key the
UFI table is a 0/1 mask, on which `bc2trans` is the identity (`bc2trans(1)=1.0`).
So `TranscriptCounts == UFICounts` elementwise, verified. Nine TSVs of each are
still written; use `ReadCounts`.

### Comparing the two protocols' rRNA under one strand flag
Rejected as the headline. VASA's forward-strand share of ribosomal reads is
**76.1%**, FLASH-seq's ~**50%**, so no single flag treats both fairly: `y`
discards 23.9% of one and 50.6% of the other. All three pairings are reported
(4.50× / 6.08× / 8.95×) with each protocol's own correct flag as the headline.

### `filt_unigenes=y` on step 7 for the ten-library run
Rejected. The threshold is `ncells = max(5, round(0.01*ncols))`, written for a
384-cell plate. At 10 libraries it demands 50% of them, and at 1 it demands 5 of
1, so no gene passes and `reduceGeneName` silently loses its "exactly one
component is a known unigene" rule.

### `module load quarto/1.5.57-x64` to render this document
Does not work on this host as of 2026-07-29: `ERROR: Unable to locate a modulefile
for 'quarto/1.5.57-x64'`. The binary exists at
`/camp/apps/eb/software/quarto/1.5.57-x64/bin/quarto` (reports `1.5.57`) and is
invoked by full path in `render_runbook_direct.sh`. Worth fixing in the
`reproducible-runbook` skill, which documents the module form.

### Attributing the `check` stage's 20/20 `MISS` to a filesystem outage
**Retracted.** The `check` stage reported `MISS` for all 10 libraries in both arms
on 2026-07-28 21:03 and does not reproduce — it now returns `OK` for all 10 in
each arm, and `find_r1` reproduced step by step gives `n=1`, rc=0. Two wrong
explanations were published before that: first that the glob missed the lane field
(it does not — `ZHA8833A9_S*_R1_001.fastq.gz` matches
`ZHA8833A9_S108_L007_R1_001.fastq.gz` uniquely, and the `ls` cited as evidence
used a broader pattern), then that the delivery filesystem was briefly unreadable
(never tested; the corroborating files cited do not exist at that path). **Cause
remains unknown.** To diagnose it the `check` stage needs to log `find`'s exit
status and a `stat` of `$FSV_FASTQ` on failure — a retrospective diagnosis is not
available because that evidence was never captured.
